newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan says Taleban accept northern foe's terms.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan says Taleban accept northern foe's terms.

text.p: Pakistan said on Thursday that Afghanistan's Taleban had accepted peace proposals made by northern opposition leader General Abdul Malik, who handed the Islamic militia a stinging defeat in the north last week.

A Pakistani Foreign Ministry spokesman told a weekly news briefing that Malik had given the Taleban three conditions for a peace deal, which he passed to the Pakistani consul-general in the northern capital of Mazar-i-Sharif.

The spokesman said Malik had demanded that the Taleban leave an opposition alliance to rule the north, stop trying to disarm opposition fighters there and agree to an "Islamic dispensation" that Malik would set up in cooperation with the Taleban.

The spokesman said the Taleban leadership, including the movement's Kandahar-based chief Mullah Mohammad Omar, had told Pakistan on Saturday that they had agreed to all Malik's proposals. He said the Taleban were now awaiting Malik's reply.

Malik defected to the Taleban last month in a mutiny against former opposition leader General Abdul Rashid Dostum, but switched sides again after Taleban fighters entered Mazar-i-Sharif and began enforcing their strict Islamic code.
Malik's ethnic Uzbek troops linked up with Shi'ite Moslem militiamen to drive the Taleban out of the city in street battles that cost the Taleban an estimated 300 dead.
